chapter: Serenading and playing with Buddy Bolden
title: Dandy Lewis, Frankie Duson and the Eagle Band
summary: Bass player Dandy Lewis worked with Frankie Duson's very hot Eagle Band; Duson's trombone style compared with Jim Robinson; Willie Cornish's wife.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: He used to tell me about Dandy Lewis. Do you remember Dandy Lewis? The bass player?
Yeah. He used to play with Frankie Dueson. Oh, yeah.
Eagle Band.
That was a...
What kind of band was that? A real smooth band?
Mm-hmm. That was a hot band.
Hot band?
No, very hot.
How did Frankie Dueson sound? How did Frankie Dueson sound? Would he sound... How would he compare, say, with Roy Palmer or Kid R.A.? Did he sound like Jim Robinson or who?
He played hard, pretty hard. He played like Jim... He played like Jim... He played like Jim Robinson. Yeah?
Hard. That one rocked right in. Yeah.
Do you know Roy Palmer? I never met him.
I used to try to imitate him when I had a trombone. But I couldn't tell him. Because you didn't hear that. Not Roy Palmer. He was too old. Willie Carnish? I knew you didn't know about him.
No, but I knew his young wife.
Hmm.
She used to live on Bertrand Street. No, Bolivar Street, I believe it was. Right around Tulane Avenue. You know where Tulane and Bolivar is? That neighborhood.
What do you mean? Here in the church. What do you mean?
Tulane and Bolivar?
Yeah. That's what you're trying to call it? A block and a half. What do you call him? Bertrand? That's Bolivar. That's Bolivar. Ballivar.
Ballivar. Ballivar. Ballivar. Ballivar.
Ballivar. Ballivar.
Ballivar. Ballivar.
Ballivar. Ballivar.
Ballivar.
Ballivar.
Yeah, I mean, you get him right, you know, tell him that, and he knew that.
Yeah.
